question: What happens to routine childhood vaccines when they are exposed to extreme heat?

options.A: It extends the official expiration date
options.B: It changes the liquid vaccine into a solid gel
options.C: It permanently destroys their active components
options.D: It causes the glass vial to crack and leak

explanation: Heat breaks down the biological elements inside vaccines so they can no longer stimulate the immune system, and this damage cannot be reversed. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is keeping vaccines cold so challenging for midwives working in rural Nigerian primary health clinics?

options.A: Vaccines manufactured in Nigeria require freezing instead of cooling
options.B: Frequent electricity cuts and high ambient tropical temperatures
options.C: Rural health posts are forbidden from using modern refrigerators
options.D: Mothers refuse to bring babies to clinics with cold storage

explanation: Hot weather combined with unreliable power supply puts constant pressure on storage equipment to keep vaccines cold. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which of these routine vaccines is severely damaged if it accidentally freezes inside the refrigerator?
explanation: Pentavalent contains aluminum adjuvants that clump together when frozen, which ruins the vaccine and can cause severe soreness at the injection site. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h2)

question: A midwife finds that the vaccine fridge temperature dropped to -2°C overnight. What should she do with the liquid TT and pentavalent stock?

options.A: Perform the shake test to check for ice damage before using
options.B: Keep using them since freezing only affects live viral vaccines
options.C: Administer them immediately before they warm up further
options.D: Heat the vials gently in warm water to restore the liquid state

explanation: The shake test helps determine if freezing has ruined the adjuvant structure in liquid, freeze-sensitive vaccines. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why shouldn't midwives use standard household refrigerators to store vaccines in a health facility?

options.A: Their internal temperatures fluctuate wildly and lack precise control
options.B: They are too small to hold standard immunisation supplies
options.C: They can only operate using direct solar panel connections
options.D: They consume too much fuel for the clinic generator

explanation: Household fridges have uneven cooling zones and defrost cycles that can accidentally freeze or overheat vaccines. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h3)

question: What makes Solar Direct Drive (SDD) refrigerators so helpful for remote Nigerian health posts?

options.A: They automatically reconstitute dry vaccine vials
options.B: They double as domestic food freezers for staff members
options.C: They require no sunlight during the entire rainy season
options.D: They operate without expensive or fragile battery storage banks

explanation: SDD units use solar energy directly to freeze water linings, eliminating reliance on short-lived batteries that frequently fail in rural clinics. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h3)

question: How often does a midwife need to check and record the temperature of the vaccine storage refrigerator?

options.A: Once a week during monthly meetings
options.B: Only when a power outage occurs
options.C: Once a month during stock audits

explanation: Checking temperatures twice a day catches equipment failures early before entire batches of vaccines spoil. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why do midwives place water-filled plastic bottles at the bottom of an ice-lined vaccine refrigerator?

options.A: To freeze solid and act as unconditioned ice packs for outreach
options.B: To provide drinking water for staff during hot clinic shifts
options.C: To help stabilize and hold the cold temperature during power failures
options.D: To increase humidity levels inside the vaccine storage chamber

explanation: Water bottles add thermal mass, slowing down how fast the internal cabinet warms up when electricity cuts off. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h4)

question: What does it mean if the inner square of a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) is darker than the outer circle?

options.A: The vaccine has frozen and formed ice crystals
options.B: The vaccine has suffered heat damage and must be discarded
options.C: The vaccine expiry date has been extended
options.D: The vaccine is brand new and has maximum potency

explanation: A darkened inner square indicates cumulative heat exposure that ruins the vaccine, meaning it cannot be administered. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h5)

question: How does the FEFO principle guide daily stock management in a midwifery clinic?

options.A: Newer shipments are always used before older inventory
options.B: Freezer-safe vials are kept separate from heat-sensitive ones
options.C: Vaccines expiring sooner are used before those expiring later
options.D: Vaccines brought back from outreach are discarded first

explanation: FEFO (First Expire, First Out) prevents valuable medicine from spoiling on the shelf past its expiration date. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h5)

question: A midwife arrives at the clinic and finds the fridge temperature is +15°C because the generator broke. What is her immediate first step?

options.A: Wait for the generator to be repaired before checking vaccines
options.B: Leave the refrigerator door open to let heat escape quickly
options.C: Transfer vaccines into a cold box with conditioned ice packs
options.D: Discard all the vaccine vials into the medical waste bin

explanation: Moving endangered stock into a temporary cold box preserves their thermal safety while the main appliance is being fixed. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h6)

question: Who should a midwife contact immediately after a major cold chain failure at a primary health post?
explanation: The LIO coordinates district logistics, helps arrange emergency replacement stock, and dispatches technicians. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h6)
